significance.root_decision: For every even n the Bender–Knuth involutions generate the full symmetric group on the linear extensions of the zigzag poset Z_n (whose number is an Euler number: 5, 61, 1385, ...). The source verified n ≤ 10 by computer and proved only transitivity. The proof is an induction on n: removing the last two elements embeds the action for n − 2, and a commutator of moves supported on different blocks isolates a 3-cycle; the group is primitive because a block containing one fibre is forced to be everything, so Jordan's theorem gives the alternating group; finally the second Bender–Knuth move is an odd permutation, by a sign recurrence through the tail fibres. Lean defines Z_n literally (an even-indexed element is below its neighbours), linear extensions as position-to-vertex bijections respecting the order, the Bender–Knuth move as the swap of adjacent positions when the two elements are incomparable (proved equivalent to the literal rule), and checks the counts 5 and 61 so that the statement cannot hold by an empty or trivial set.
significance.caveat: The Lean route differs from the original written proof in two places (block propagation plus Jordan's theorem instead of normal-closure support propagation; a tail sign recurrence instead of Euler-number congruences); the revised paper follows the Lean route. The citation index was enumerated through OpenAlex only. The formalization took eight stages, two of them in parallel. Cross-model confidence 0.80, not routine 0.80. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the final theorem and every definition with the endpoint the Claude Opus reviewer had written (same statement; ZigzagLE an abbreviation of the required subtype; the move proved equal to the literal incomparability swap), and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check confirmed the full symmetric groups S_5, S_61 and S_1385 for n = 4, 6, 8 by independent computation.
